<div class="definition-block" style="background: #f8f9fa; border-left: 4px solid #FF9900; padding: 24px 32px; margin: 32px 0 48px 0; border-radius: 0 8px 8px 0;">

**Trade-specific quantity surveying** provides specialist cost estimation for individual construction trades rather than generic whole-building estimates. Applying hands-on trade knowledge -- drylining systems, structural concrete and steelwork, facade cladding, fire protection, and MEP infrastructure -- trade-specific estimation catches the specialist items, allowances, and waste factors that generalist QS approaches routinely miss. BIM Takeoff prices these trades directly, checking quantities against the drawings and specification by hand.

</div>

## 4 Specialist Areas of Expertise

::: {.specialist-areas style="margin: 48px 0;"}

::: {.specialist-card}
### <i class="bi bi-grid-3x3-gap-fill" style="color: var(--bim-orange); margin-right: 12px;" aria-hidden="true"></i>Drylining & Partitions

#### What We Cover
- Metal stud framing systems (Knauf, Gyproc, Siniat)
- Plasterboard installation (standard, fire-rated, acoustic, moisture-resistant)
- Suspended ceilings (exposed grid, concealed, acoustic panels)
- Acoustic treatments and STC/Rw ratings
- Fire-rated partitions and compartmentation

#### Our Experience
- Drylining projects estimated across offices, warehouses, and residential developments
- Worked with Knauf, British Gypsum, CSR Gyprock specifications
- Understand labour rates: crew sizing, productivity factors, site access constraints
- Know material waste factors vary with ceiling heights and cutting requirements

#### Typical Package Scope
- Full BOQ with material specifications
- Labour hours by system type, with allowance for fire-rated specifications
- Equipment/scaffolding requirements
- Testing and certification costs (fire ratings, acoustic performance)
- Warranty and defects liability

#### Critical Knowledge
::: {style="padding: 16px; background: #f8f9fa; border-left: 4px solid var(--bim-orange); margin: 16px 0;"}
- Acoustic sealant is often missed from the material cost
- Fire-rated systems slow installation
- Height work reduces productivity
- Curved walls increase material waste
:::

**Deliverable:** Detailed estimate with installation sequence, material schedule, labour allocation
:::

::: {.specialist-card}
### <i class="bi bi-fire" style="color: var(--bim-orange); margin-right: 12px;" aria-hidden="true"></i>Fire Protection Systems

#### What We Cover
- Passive fire protection (compartmentation, fire stopping, intumescent coatings)
- Active fire systems (sprinklers, detection, suppression)
- Fire-rated doors, windows, and penetrations
- Fire curtains and smoke control systems
- Structural fire protection (steel/concrete coatings)

#### Our Experience
- Fire protection packages estimated across warehouses, data centres, and high-rise
- Compliance with AS 1530.4, BS 476, EN 13501, Polish regulations
- Worked with Trafalgar, Hilti, Nullifire, FireMaster, Rockwool, Titan systems
- Understand certification requirements: 3rd party testing, BCA/NCC compliance
- Know labour complexity: confined spaces, sequential installation, coordination

#### Typical Package Scope
- Fire strategy review and compartmentation schedule
- Material specifications with fire ratings (FRL 60/60/60, 90/90/90, etc.)
- Installation labour with access/coordination factors
- Testing and commissioning (smoke tests, pressure tests)
- Authority approvals and certification documentation

#### Critical Knowledge
::: {style="padding: 16px; background: #f8f9fa; border-left: 4px solid var(--bim-orange); margin: 16px 0;"}
- Fire ratings ≠ installation costs
- Penetration sealing is priced per penetration, not per square metre
- Intumescent coatings: surface preparation is a significant share of total cost
- Testing and certification can add meaningfully to package value
- Coordination with other trades is critical for sequencing
:::

**Deliverable:** Fire protection cost estimate with compliance roadmap
:::

::: {.specialist-card}
### <i class="bi bi-building" style="color: var(--bim-orange); margin-right: 12px;" aria-hidden="true"></i>Facades & Cladding

#### What We Cover
- Rainscreen cladding systems (terracotta, fiber cement, metal panels)
- Curtain wall systems (unitized, stick-built)
- Insulated panels (PIR, mineral wool, sandwich panels)
- Facade access systems (BMU, gantries, cradles)
- Weatherproofing and sealant systems

#### Our Experience
- Facade projects estimated across warehouses, offices, and high-rise residential
- Material systems: Kingspan, Trespa, Equitone, Alucobond, Cemintel
- Understanding wind loading calculations and structural integration
- Complex installation sequences: scaffolding, craneage, weather delays
- Know that metal panel pricing carries real market volatility risk

#### Typical Package Scope
- Facade BOQ by elevation and system type
- Substructure (rails, brackets, fixings) fully detailed
- Labour by height zone
- Access equipment (scaffolding, BMU hire, safety systems)
- Testing (water penetration, air tightness, thermal performance)

#### Critical Knowledge
::: {style="padding: 16px; background: #f8f9fa; border-left: 4px solid var(--bim-orange); margin: 16px 0;"}
- Facades carry a disproportionate share of tender risk relative to their cost
- Installation speed depends heavily on system complexity
- Weather delays need a realistic contingency allowance
- Sealant replacement should be budgeted for future remedial works
- Access equipment is a meaningful part of installation cost
:::

**Deliverable:** Facade cost estimate with installation methodology
:::

::: {.specialist-card}
### <i class="bi bi-diagram-3" style="color: var(--bim-orange); margin-right: 12px;" aria-hidden="true"></i>Structural Works

#### What We Cover
- Structural steel (frames, trusses, bracing)
- Reinforced concrete (suspended slabs, columns, cores)
- Post-tensioned slabs and beams
- FRP (fiber-reinforced polymer) strengthening
- Structural connections and tolerances

#### Our Experience
- Structural packages estimated across warehouses, bridges, high-rise, and houses
- Steel: fabrication + erection + painting + fire protection
- Concrete: formwork + reinforcement + pour + cure + finish
- Complex calculations: load paths, connection detailing, construction sequences
- Material pricing: rebar = commodity risk, structural steel = fabrication lead times

#### Typical Package Scope
- Structural steel schedule (tonnage, connection types, erection sequence)
- Concrete schedule (volumes, reinforcement density, formwork complexity)
- Testing requirements (NDT, load testing, concrete strength)
- Temporary works (propping, scaffolding, safety systems)
- Coordination with MEP and architectural trades

#### Critical Knowledge
::: {style="padding: 16px; background: #f8f9fa; border-left: 4px solid var(--bim-orange); margin: 16px 0;"}
- Structural steel cost splits across fabrication, erection, and painting/fire protection
- Post-tensioned slabs cost more in material but build faster
- Connection complexity drives price: a simple connection costs far less than a moment connection
- Concrete pump hire is a day-rate cost including operator
- Reinforcement fixing labour is priced per tonne
:::

**Deliverable:** Structural cost estimate with construction methodology
:::

:::

## Our Proven Specialist Estimating Process

::: {.process-timeline style="margin: 48px 0; padding: 40px; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #f8f9fa 0%, #ffffff 100%); border-radius: 12px;"}

::: {.process-step style="margin-bottom: 32px; padding-left: 32px; border-left: 3px solid var(--bim-orange);"}
#### Step 1: Trade-Specific Scope Definition

**Duration:** 2-3 days

**What We Do:**
- Deep-dive review of drawings and specifications
- Identify trade-specific complexities (fire ratings, acoustic requirements, wind loads)
- Assess installation constraints (access, sequencing, coordination)
- Define exact scope boundaries and interfaces with other trades

**Free sample takeoff:** send one floor, one elevation or one unit type and we measure it at no charge.

**Key Output:** Scope clarification document with identified complexities
:::

::: {.process-step style="margin-bottom: 32px; padding-left: 32px; border-left: 3px solid var(--bim-orange);"}
#### Step 2: Specialist Material Takeoff

**Duration:** 2-4 days

**What We Do:**
- Measure quantities with trade-specific care
- Include waste factors appropriate to the system type
- Identify long-lead items and procurement risks
- Verify material compatibility and approval requirements

**Deliverable:** Detailed BOQ with manufacturer specifications
:::

::: {.process-step style="margin-bottom: 32px; padding-left: 32px; border-left: 3px solid var(--bim-orange);"}
#### Step 3: Installation Labour Analysis

**Duration:** 2-3 days

**What We Do:**
- Calculate crew sizes and productivity rates
- Factor in complexity multipliers for fire-rated systems and height access
- Include access equipment and temporary works
- Account for weather delays and site constraints

**Deliverable:** Labour schedule with resource allocation
:::

::: {.process-step style="margin-bottom: 32px; padding-left: 32px; border-left: 3px solid var(--bim-orange);"}
#### Step 4: Compliance & Testing Budget

**Duration:** 1-2 days

**What We Do:**
- Identify testing requirements (fire ratings, structural load tests, facade testing)
- Budget for certifications and authority approvals
- Include quality control and commissioning
- Factor in warranty and defects liability periods

**Deliverable:** Compliance cost schedule

**Often Missed:** testing and certification costs, budgeted from the start
:::

::: {.process-step style="margin-bottom: 32px; padding-left: 32px; border-left: 3px solid var(--bim-orange);"}
#### Step 5: Risk Assessment & Contingency

**Duration:** 1 day

**What We Do:**
- Identify material price volatility risks
- Assess installation risks (weather, access, coordination)
- Calculate appropriate contingency depending on package complexity
- Provide value engineering alternatives

**Deliverable:** Complete specialist estimate with risk register
:::

::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: 32px; padding: 24px; background: var(--bim-charcoal); color: var(--bim-white); border-radius: 8px;"}
**Total Timeline:** 8-13 working days | **Project Duration:** 2-3 weeks from start to finish

**Fast-Track Available:** Urgent estimates in 5-7 working days, for an agreed surcharge
:::
:::

## Frequently Asked Questions

::: {.faq-section}

::: {.faq-item}
::: {.faq-question}
**Q: What makes specialist trade estimating different from general estimating?**
:::
::: {.faq-answer}
A: Specialist estimators have hands-on installation experience and understand the nuances that affect costs: fire-rated systems require specific installation sequences, facade work is weather-dependent, and structural connections have hidden complexity. We account for factors that generic estimators often miss.
:::
:::

::: {.faq-item}
::: {.faq-question}
**Q: Do you work with specific material systems only?**
:::
::: {.faq-answer}
A: No. We have experience with all major systems (Knauf, Gyproc, Siniat, Kingspan, Trespa, Hilti, etc.) and can estimate any manufacturer's products. Our expertise is in understanding the installation and performance characteristics, not brand loyalty. We often provide value engineering alternatives using different systems.
:::
:::

::: {.faq-item}
::: {.faq-question}
**Q: Can you estimate supply-only packages?**
:::
::: {.faq-answer}
A: Yes. We provide estimates for supply-only, install-only, or complete supply & install packages. Each requires different considerations for waste factors, logistics, and risk allocation. Supply-only and install packages carry different waste allowances depending on complexity.
:::
:::

::: {.faq-item}
::: {.faq-question}
**Q: How do you handle compliance requirements?**
:::
::: {.faq-answer}
A: We budget for all testing, certification, and approval costs from the start. This includes fire ratings (AS 1530.4, BS 476, EN 13501), structural load testing, facade performance testing, and authority approvals. These costs are frequently missed in generic estimates.
:::
:::

::: {.faq-item}
::: {.faq-question}
**Q: What information do you need to provide an estimate?**
:::
::: {.faq-answer}
A: Ideally: architectural drawings, specifications, material preferences, and any performance requirements (fire ratings, acoustic performance, wind loads). For complex projects, we may request structural drawings and coordination plans. We can work with preliminary information and refine as details become available.
:::
:::

::: {.faq-item}
::: {.faq-question}
**Q: Do you provide value engineering alternatives?**
:::
::: {.faq-answer}
A: Absolutely. Every specialist estimate includes value engineering recommendations: alternative material systems, installation methods, and performance-equivalent substitutions that can reduce costs without compromising quality.
:::
:::

::: {.faq-item}
::: {.faq-question}
**Q: What project sizes do you handle?**
:::
::: {.faq-answer}
A: We work on projects from small fit-outs (500 sqm) to large-scale developments (50,000+ sqm). Specialist trade complexity matters more than overall project size—a high-rise facade is more complex than a large warehouse drylining package. A minimum fee applies to smaller projects. Priced per package, quoted before we start. No hourly billing and no fee for scope we did not agree.
:::
:::

::: {.faq-item}
::: {.faq-question}
**Q: Do you support tendering processes?**
:::
::: {.faq-answer}
A: Yes. We provide full tender support: quantity take-off, detailed cost breakdown, risk analysis, bid document preparation, and contractor evaluation. Our estimates give you confidence in your tender submissions. We can also attend tender interviews and negotiations.
:::
:::

::: {.faq-item}
::: {.faq-question}
**Q: How quickly can you provide an estimate?**
:::
::: {.faq-answer}
A: Standard timeline is 2-3 weeks for comprehensive specialist estimates. For urgent requirements, we offer a fast-track service (5-7 working days) for an agreed surcharge. Initial budget estimates can be provided within 48 hours for feasibility studies.
:::
:::

::: {.faq-item}
::: {.faq-question}
**Q: Do you work internationally?**
:::
::: {.faq-answer}
A: Yes. While based in Poland, we have extensive experience with EU, UK, and Australian standards. We've completed projects across Europe, Asia-Pacific, and the Middle East. Our estimates include location factors for labour and material costs.
:::
:::

:::
